author: Riley Johnson
title: Watch Virginia's restored elk herd live on the elk cam in Buchanan - NewsBreak
text:
By Riley Johnson No media credit provided. ,
8 hours ago
BUCHANAN COUNTY, Va. ( WFXR ) – The Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources (VDWR) is entering its eighth season of providing the Virginia Elk Cam on its website.
VDWR says the restored elk herd, often referred to as Appalachia’s Greatest Conservation Success Story, is now available for you to view on your phone, tablet, or computer anytime through December.
According to officials, the camera, located on reclaimed mine land in Buchanan County, scans a field frequented by elk, especially during early morning, evening, and nighttime hours.
As the weather begins to cool, the elk will become more active during the day. However, according to the website, the best times to view elk are early mornings and late evenings.
VDWR suggests turning up the volume for the opportunity to hear elk bugling during the breeding season in October.
Virginia State Parks open for hunting to manage deer population Elk were historically found throughout eastern North America, including Virginia, according to VDWR. However, by the late 1800s, unregulated hunting and habitat alteration resulted in the eradication of elk in the East. Officials say the last survivor of Virginia’s original elk herd was killed in 1855 in Clarke County.
According to officials, 75 elk were relocated into Buchanan County, Virginia, between 2012 and 2014, from eastern Kentucky. The herd has now grown to more than 250. These captivating creatures also share the landscape with other wildlife that VDWR says appear on the camera as well, such as deer and turkeys, as well as the occasional black bear, coyote, and more.
